body:
CONTEXT
Generated files (lockfiles, dist/, minified bundles) can fill the review payload and crowd out real changes. Release 2.11.1 has no way to exclude paths.

GOAL
An OPT-IN, repeatable `--exclude <glob>` that removes matching paths from the review payload in working-tree and branch scope, and reports what it removed. Without the flag, behavior is byte-identical to 2.11.1 (no default exclusion set), so the 3.0.0 parity suite is unaffected.

DECISIONS (P0, 2026-10-07)
- Opt-in only. There is no default set; one may be proposed later as a numbered 3.0.0 delta.
- Reporting: when any path matches, print one stderr line "Excluded N file(s) by --exclude: <comma-separated paths>", and append each excluded path to coverage.files_skipped in the emitted result (JSON and human report) as "<path> (excluded by --exclude)". No schema change: files_skipped is already an array of strings.
- --exclude combined with --input is a usage error (exit 1, stderr names both flags), because excluding a file the user named explicitly is contradictory.

IMPLEMENTATION
1. src/utils.js parseArgs: --exclude <glob> and --exclude=<glob>, repeatable, each value may be a comma list; collected into args.exclude (string[]). Add it to the help text. Reject an empty glob as a usage error. Add the --input conflict.
2. src/git-context.js: collectReviewContext accepts an `exclude` option (globs matched against repo-relative POSIX paths by a small built-in matcher supporting *, **, ? and a trailing / for directories; no new dependency). Excluded paths are removed BEFORE diffs and file bodies are collected (each user glob is TRANSLATED to a git pathspec before use: a trailing-slash directory glob 'x/' becomes ':(exclude,glob)x/**', and any other glob g becomes ':(exclude,glob)'+g. The translated pathspecs are passed to every git call collectWorkingTree and collectBranch make (status, diff --cached, diff, ls-files --others, diff --shortstat, and the range diff/name-only/stat calls). Excluded untracked files are skipped when reading bodies. Verified in a temp repo: git pathspec ':(exclude,glob)dist/' does NOT exclude dist/app.js, while 'dist/**' does. excludedFiles is computed by the built-in matcher over the unfiltered changed-file list, and the built-in matcher is the semantic authority), so excluded content never enters the payload or counts toward --max-files/--max-bytes. Return excludedFiles (sorted).
3. bin/cli.js: pass args.exclude into collectReviewContext, print the stderr line when excludedFiles is non-empty, and pass excludedFiles on to result rendering.
4. src/review.js: append the excluded paths to coverage.files_skipped (de-duplicated) in the final result, in both the single and multi-provider paths.
5. README (flags section) and a CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Added entry.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
AC1 parseArgs: "--exclude a --exclude b,c" gives ["a","b","c"]; "--exclude=" and a bare "--exclude" are usage errors; "--exclude x --input f" exits 1 naming both flags. Verified in test/utils.test.js.
AC2 End to end, working tree: in a repo with changed src/a.js and package-lock.json, running with "--exclude package-lock.json --prompt-only" prints a prompt that contains src/a.js content and NOT package-lock.json content. Negative control: the same run without --exclude contains both. Verified in test/git-context.test.js (spawning bin/cli.js).
AC3 Branch scope: the same check with "--scope branch --base main". Verified in test/git-context.test.js.
AC4 Excluded bytes do not count: a 300 KB excluded file plus a small real change stays inline (does not trip --max-bytes summary mode). Verified in test/git-context.test.js.
AC5 Reporting: a review run with a mock provider and "--exclude dist/" prints "Excluded 1 file(s) by --exclude: dist/app.js" on stderr, and the --json result's coverage.files_skipped contains "dist/app.js (excluded by --exclude)". Without the flag there is no such line and no such entry. Verified in test/review.test.js.
AC6 Glob matcher unit tests: "*.lock" matches yarn.lock and not a/yarn.lock.bak; "dist/" matches dist/x.js and dist/a/b.js; "**/*.min.js" matches a/b/c.min.js. Verified in test/git-context.test.js.
AC9 Matcher and pathspec agree: for a fixed corpus of paths (yarn.lock, a/yarn.lock, a/yarn.lock.bak, dist/x.js, dist/a/b.js, distx/y.js, a/b/c.min.js, c.min.js), each of the globs "*.lock", "**/*.lock", "dist/", "**/*.min.js" selects the same set via the built-in matcher as via `git ls-files -- . ':(exclude,glob)<translated>'` complement in a temp repo containing those files. Verified in test/git-context.test.js. Negative control: passing the untranslated 'dist/' pathspec makes the comparison fail.
AC7 No behavior change without the flag: the existing test suite passes unchanged (npm test).
AC8 README and CHANGELOG are updated; test/utils.test.js asserts README.md mentions --exclude.

SEQUENCING NOTE
T18 edits bin/cli.js and src/review.js, which the 3.0.0 step-1 refactor (T55/T56/T57) rewrites. T18 must merge BEFORE T55 starts. T55 then carries T18 forward, and T18's tests must stay green through C2/C1.

VERIFICATION COMMAND
npm test
title: Add opt-in --exclude <glob> so generated artifacts do not dominate the review payload
